plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch covariate
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12,000 gene x 12 sample raw integer count matrix from salmon (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv: sample, condition, batch). The design is 6 treated vs 6 control human kidney samples split across two known processing batches, each batch holding both conditions. Because the batch is known and balanced across conditions, the correct handling is a fixed-effect design term (~ batch + condition) rather than any pre-correction of the counts — adjusting counts before the test would inflate confidence in the downstream inference. T1S1 runs sample-structure QC on a blind VST (PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes), colouring by both condition and batch, so the size of the batch effect and any outlier sample is known before the model runs. T1S2 fits the DESeq2 negative-binomial model with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, an explicitly set reference level so that a positive log2FC means higher in treated, a Wald test on the condition coefficient, apeglm shrinkage for reporting and ranking, and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering; the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted. T1S3 repeats the same design with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as a robustness check — at 6 replicates per group the two tools agree on most genes but not all, and the intersection is the high-confidence set. T2S1 runs fgsea preranked on the full list of tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed ranking-metric choice is resolved in favour of the Wald statistic: it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike an unshrunken fold change or a saturating signed p-value), against MSigDB human hallmark first and the human Reactome pathway sets second. T1S4 consolidates everything into one report with the fit diagnostics, the gene tables carrying both the shrunken and the unshrunken effect with its standard error, the leading-edge genes of each significant set, and a full reproducibility record. Twelve samples with six per group is adequate but not large: the analysis will find strong, consistent effects and will miss small ones, and that limit is to be stated rather than papered over.

Low count pre-filter: at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples
DESeq2 design ~ batch + condition with explicit reference level control
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness check on the same design
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Consolidated report: fit diagnostics, gene tables with shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading-edge genes, reproducibility record

steps.question: Which hallmark and Reactome pathways are coordinately shifted between treated and control kidney samples, and which genes form the leading edge of each?
steps.description: Run fgsea preranked on the FULL list of genes tested in T1S2 — not a thresholded subset — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column). The ranking-metric dispute is resolved here in favour of the Wald statistic because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike an unshrunken fold change (noisy at low counts) or a signed p-value (which ties at saturation); state this choice in the output. Drop genes with an NA statistic and report how many were dropped. Test first against the human MSigDB hallmark gene sets, then against the human Reactome pathway gene sets as the second collection; both are gene-symbol collections, so the ranked list stays in HGNC symbol space and no identifier conversion is needed — if a mapping step is nonetheless used, report the unmapped share and never mix identifier spaces between the list and the sets. Restrict Reactome to the Homo sapiens pathways using the accompanying pathway index before testing. Apply a set size window of 15 to 500 genes computed after intersecting each set with the tested genes, BH-adjust across sets within each collection separately, set and record an explicit random seed for the permutations, and collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea collapsePathways) reporting one representative per group with the full table kept as a supplement. For every significant set, output the leading-edge genes with their Wald statistic, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. If fewer than about 50 genes reached padj < 0.05 in T1S2, do NOT additionally run an over-representation test on that short list — say so and rely on the ranked result.
steps.context: Human kidney, treated vs control. The reference store currently holds an MSigDB human hallmark symbol GMT (50 sets) and a Reactome pathway GMT with a species index; both are needed here. If either is absent at run time, report which collection was missing and run the ranked test on whichever human pathway collection is available, naming it.
acceptance_criteria: Input is the full ranked vector of all tested genes from T1S2 ranked by the Wald statistic; the number of genes ranked and the number dropped for NA statistics are reported
Ranking metric is stated explicitly in the output as the DESeq2 Wald statistic, with the reason for the choice
Hallmark human gene sets tested first, human Reactome pathway sets second, each with its collection name and version recorded
Set size window 15-500 applied after intersecting with the tested genes; BH adjustment applied within each collection
A random seed is set and recorded for the fgsea permutations
Redundant significant sets collapsed, with one representative per group reported and the full table retained
Leading-edge genes listed per significant set with their gene-level statistic, and leading-edge overlap between reported sets marked
If fewer than ~50 genes passed padj < 0.05 in T1S2, an over-representation test is explicitly NOT run and the reason is stated
constraints: Rank the FULL tested gene list — never cut it at an adjusted p-value or a fold change before the test
Use the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric; do not rank by the unshrunken log2 fold change alone and do not use a signed p-value with ties
Use human gene sets only — the store also holds mouse and rat collections and a species mismatch fails silently as an empty result
Filter the Reactome GMT to Homo sapiens pathways via its pathway index before testing
Apply the 15-500 size window after intersecting each set with the tested genes, and report the window
Set an explicit random seed for the permutation p-values and record it
If a required pathway collection is not present in the reference store at run time, report its absence explicitly rather than substituting a different organism or silently skipping the collection
caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent — a ranked test and an over-representation test on the same data give different lists; present a set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven finding
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment of count data; the ranked test on the tested-gene universe mitigates but does not eliminate this
Reactome sets are hierarchical and overlap heavily, so a block of significant child pathways is one finding, not many — this is why collapsing is required

grounding.reason: Ranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment (R-0107, R-0045); disputed rule R-0108 resolved to the Wald statistic per R-0099; human order is Hallmark then Reactome (R-0048, R-0098); size window and collapsing per R-0047 and R-0052; short-list ORA suppressed per R-0103.

steps.name: Consolidated DE and pathway report
steps.question: What is the reproducible, fully-specified answer to which genes and pathways differ between treated and control kidney samples, and how much confidence does the design support?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Lead with the method (DESeq2 Wald on ~ batch + condition with apeglm shrinkage, edgeR quasi-likelihood as the second method), every package version, the design formula, the contrast written as condition / treated / control, the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, and the number of differentially expressed genes. Place the two fit diagnostics before the gene tables: the MA plot with significant genes marked, and the dispersion-estimate plot with the fitted trend. Include the QC evidence from T1S1 on whether batch drove the leading variance axis and how much of it the design term absorbed. The gene table carries, per gene, baseMean, the unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue and padj; rank genes and draw plots on the SHRUNKEN value and name the shrinkage estimator in the header. Add a volcano plot and a heatmap of the top genes on VST values with condition and batch annotation. Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3 as the high-confidence set. Report the enrichment from T2S1 with the collection name and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the tool version and the multiple-testing method, plus the leading-edge genes per significant set, and state explicitly that enrichment results depend on the method chosen. Close with a limitations paragraph naming the sample size (6 per group), the batch structure, the p-value histogram shape, the count of outlier-flagged NA genes, and what effect sizes this design could not have detected. Attach the full reproducibility record: sessionInfo, every package version, the random seeds used, and the version of each gene set collection.
steps.context: Final synthesis across T1S1 (QC), T1S2 (DESeq2), T1S3 (edgeR overlap) and T2S1 (fgsea). No new statistical inference is performed here.
acceptance_criteria: Report names the method, all package versions, the design formula ~ batch + condition, the contrast as treated over control, the thresholds, the number of genes tested and the number differentially expressed
MA plot and dispersion plot both appear before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows
Gene table contains baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange (estimator named), stat, pvalue, padj; ranking and plots use the shrunken value
Volcano plot and top-gene VST heatmap annotated by condition and batch are included
DESeq2/edgeR significant counts and their intersection are reported as the high-confidence set
Enrichment section states collection and version, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool version and adjustment method, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set
A limitations paragraph names the 6-per-group sample size, the batch handling, the p-value histogram shape, and the number of outlier-flagged NA genes
Reproducibility record attached: sessionInfo, package versions, seeds, gene set collection versions
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, never on the unshrunken estimate alone, and keep the unshrunken value with its standard error in the table
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit — shrinkage does not change the test
State the enrichment method dependence explicitly; present enriched sets as hypotheses for follow-up
Do not perform any new statistical test in this step
Do not overstate: if few genes reach significance, or the p-value histogram is irregular, say so in the headline rather than in a footnote
caveats: A treated-vs-control contrast in 12 samples is a screen, not a confirmation — no causal or mechanistic claim follows from it
Batch adjustment via a design term removes the mean batch shift but not batch-by-condition interaction, which this design has too few samples to test

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report procedure: method/versions/design/thresholds (R-0041), shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat (R-0051, R-0055), leading edge (R-0105), reproducibility record (R-0086).
